title: The pluperfect: what had already happened

sections.content: You know the *pluscuamperfecto* from B1 Unit 1: *había* + a past participle says that something had already happened before another moment in the past. In the history of independence, it is the tool for "by then": by the time of the crisis of 1808, what had already changed in the world?

items.spanish: En 1810 ya se habían formado juntas en varias ciudades.
items.english: By 1810, juntas had already been formed in several cities.

items.spanish: Antes de 1808, muchos criollos ya habían leído libros de la Ilustración.
items.english: Before 1808, many criollos had already read books of the Enlightenment.

items.spanish: Los americanos no habían elegido al nuevo rey.
items.english: The Americans had not chosen the new king.

items.spanish: Cuando llegó la noticia, la crisis ya había empezado en España.
items.english: When the news arrived, the crisis had already begun in Spain.

sections.content: *Ya*, *antes de* and *todavía no* often go with the pluperfect. Nothing goes between *había* and the participle (*ya había empezado*), and *se* goes before *había* (*se habían formado*).
